# Native Simscape Operating-Point Restart

## Scope and Authority

Issue #11921 establishes an R2025b native restart prerequisite. It does not
qualify a production golf model, a fitted capture, muscle recruitment or
six-engine parity. The generated fixture combines a physical mass, spring,
damper, ideal force source and position sensor with a discrete Unit Delay.
Required production model/variant rows remain visible and unqualified.

Tools #5470 owns the separately versioned opaque native artifact/envelope
contract. This native fixture currently tests MATLAB semantics independently;
it does not yet consume a published exact Tools1.1 dependency. Existing numeric
T01 state vectors cannot replace hidden Simscape state.

## Physical Model and Numerical Method

The scalar physical network uses mass 1 kg, spring stiffness 40 N/m and damping
2 N*s/m, satisfying $m \ddot{x}+c \dot{x}+k x=f(t)$. Inputs use physical seconds and
force units N. The MATLAB constructor owns model creation and explicit native
solver settings. Review effective settings, converter behavior, input
interpolation and block reduction before admitting a replay policy. No fitted
reserve, feedback or observation-based correction drives the fixture.

Compare uninterrupted native integration to a split run saved at 0.2 s and
continued to 0.4 s after MAT serialization and restoration. The native
`Simulink.op.ModelOperatingPoint` is the restart authority, including hidden
physical, block, solver and execution state. The saved native clock is retained;
never retime an operating point to zero or restore only its logged numeric view.
Restore once at the beginning of the requested replay interval; no resets are
permitted within that interval.

## Identity, Ownership and Failure Contracts

Bind actual R2025b runtime, expected native class, source/loaded model identity,
snapshot time, effective solver/configuration and exact saved input rows. Native
compatibility and decoded values must agree with the declaration. A MAT-file
hash identifies serialized bytes; it does not prove canonical semantic-state
encoding or a complete dependency closure. Shared contracts verify owned bytes
before decoding; native consumers must execute those verified bytes without
reopening a mutable caller path.

Reject missing/tampered artifacts, wrong class/model/runtime/clock, changed
solver policy, numeric-observable substitution and input-order/identity changes.
Transport equality is separate from executed input readback. Log the actual
injection boundary and declare whether it is a physical force, actuator command
or excitation. Preserve interpolation, limits, converter/filter policy and
relative-to-native clock translation. Large epoch rounding must not distort
physical intervals or an explicitly declared solver step.

## Evidence and Acceptance Limits

Native R2025b feature and physical-library probes succeeded on the owned fleet
worker. The first fixture test failed before its implementation existed. A
nontrivial-motion negative was also observed before correction. The final actual R2025b Update 5 native batch exits successfully: decoded
snapshot and resumed clock are both 0.2 s; physical position error is 0 m over
366 post-split samples, discrete error is 0 over 21 samples, and executed
converter-boundary input error is 0 N. Interpolation is explicitly ZOH with
hold-after-final behavior, converter units are N with zero derivative/filtering
policy, and block reduction is off. Missing, wrong model/time/runtime/blob/class
snapshot negatives pass. Retain source-bound native receipts and failed attempts. Successful
synthetic restart is a prerequisite and does not certify the production adapter.

Production acceptance requires complete native snapshots for every declared
model/variant, actual applied torque/excitation readback, independent full-horizon
replay, refinement checks, source/parameter readiness and the frozen private
capture protocol. World/anatomical registration, contact support and muscle
state remain separate scientific gates. All-model parity stays open.

## Reproduction and Turnover

Use explicit `C:/Program Files/MATLAB/R2025b/bin/matlab.exe` on the fleet worker
and run `test_native_simscape_restart` with an owned writable output directory.
Keep native MAT/SLX files in bounded run directories, receipt hashes in the
turnover, and preview videos in the requested Desktop preview folder. Reuse
existing runtime/checkouts; do not mutate another worker's environment or remove
borrowed Git object stores while retiring merged worktrees.

## Primary References

[MathWorks R2025b ModelOperatingPoint](https://www.mathworks.com/help/releases/R2025b/simulink/slref/simulink.op.modeloperatingpoint.html)
defines native state and the read-only snapshot clock; its logged-state view
excludes internal Simscape state.
[MathWorks R2025b Operating-Point Workflow](https://www.mathworks.com/help/releases/R2025b/simulink/ug/model-operating-point-for-faster-simulation.html)
documents compatibility, block reduction and effective solver configuration.
